answer: A nullifier registry stops sybil farms at the credential layer. Each agent derives one zero-knowledge nullifier from a unique hardware key (a TPM chip in a walnut-sized module) and posts it on-chain; duplicates are rejected, so one credential never yields two identities. Reuse attempts slash the attacker's stake. Forging 10,000 identities needs 10,000 distinct keys at ~$50 each plus labor: the attacker pays 10,000 x ($50 + time), linear in count, while an honest agent pays once for ivory-smooth registration. One cheap key buys a jade-hard identity dilution cannot erode.
